newsitem.title: USA: Hormel says material costs to remain high.
newsitem.headline: Hormel says material costs to remain high.

text.p: Hormel Foods Corp, which earlier reported increased second-quarter earnings despite high pork raw material costs and reduced supplies, said Thursday material costs will remain high in the third quarter.

"The high costs which have had a severe impact on our operations for the better part of a year are now projected to continue at least through the third quarter," said Hormel Chairman and Chief Executive Joel Johnson in a statement.
Hormel earlier said it earned $25.7 million, or $0.33 a share, compared to $24.5 million, or $0.32 a share, in last year's second quarter.
Poor conditions in the pork and turkey commodity business have existed longer than anticipated by government officials and industry observers, Hormel said.

"The decline in hog supplies forced company plants to operate below optimum levels while increased costs associated with the higher pork prices placed pressure on our ability to develop customary and acceptable margins for our products," Johnson said.
Harsh winter weather in the Midwest hurt turkey growing and processing operations at Hormel's Jennie-O Foods Inc, pushing up production costs, it said.
Hormel's Meat Products Group posted a 10.3 percent sales volume increase in the quarter.

Volume, margins and profit performance for the Foodservice Group have been strong, Hormel said. Cooked ham, roast beef, turkey and pre-cooked bacon categories all have recorded excellent sales growth.
